summary.headline: Emerald Finance Q4 FY26 net profit INR4.364 crore; management reiterates FY27 EPS target above INR7 versus INR4.36 in FY26.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 total income of INR9.76 crore against INR6.49 crore in Q4 FY25, with net profit of INR4.364 crore. FY26 total income was INR31.2 crore and net profit INR15.15 crore, though the transcript cites EPS of INR4.36 for both the quarter and the year, which needs verification. CRISIL upgraded the rating from BB+ to BBB-. Management said EWA disbursements slowed in the quarter because of market volatility, with corporate rejection rates near 60%. Several figures given on the call were inconsistent or deferred to email, including EWA revenue share, NPA breakup and the SME loan book.

segments.name: Early Wage Access (EWA)
segments.commentary: About 180-185 corporates active; 214 corporates on books as of March 31, 2026, though the 185 figure was also cited. Around 30,000+ employees covered, with 15% using EWA monthly and monthly repeat rate about 90%. Average loan INR25,000, cap INR1 lakh per transaction, and the lower of 50% of salary or INR1 lakh applies.

segments.name: Cross-sell (personal, home, gold loans, LAP)
segments.commentary: Cross-sell disbursal was about INR12 crore in Q4, now larger than EWA disbursal of INR10 crore. Yields vary by product: about 4% on personal loans, about 1% on gold loans and 1-1.25% on home loans or LAP. Most cross-sell is 100% distributed; small-ticket loans of INR4-5 lakh are booked on balance sheet.

segments.name: SME / business loans
segments.commentary: Book is INR111 crore per management. Management guided to decent growth in FY27 without a number, and expects cross-selling to EWA corporates to contribute.

segments.name: Gold loan syndication
segments.commentary: INR375 crore disbursed in Q4 through banking and NBFC partners.

guidance_outlook: FY27 EPS target: management said if all goes well, EPS should cross INR7 in FY27, versus INR4.36 in FY26; repeated in Q&A. Earlier call guidance of FY27 profit of INR32-40 crore was raised by an analyst; management did not restate that range.

Corporate additions: 150-200 companies targeted for FY27 by Talin Aggarwal, versus a later answer of 120-150 corporates per year over the next two years; management said the bare minimum is about 30 per quarter and that systems could handle 400-500 corporates in the year.
EWA disbursement growth: management pointed to continued growth at the pace of the last eight quarters, and said it could increase; no numeric disbursal guidance given.
Cost of funds: management said offers from financial institutions are being received after the CRISIL upgrade and an update would follow shortly; no reduction achieved yet as of the call.

Revenue growth: Sanjay Aggarwal said Q4 top line was about 25% higher than the prior quarter. Talin Aggarwal said FY27 profit growth would be at roughly the same pace as FY25 to FY26, subject to market conditions.
SME book: management expects decent growth in FY27 without a number, with a large proposal pipeline and cross-sell to EWA corporates.
capex_capacity: No capex or capacity figures were discussed on the call.

Platform: proprietary API-driven platform for onboarding, salary validation and disbursement; Emerald EWA mobile app rolled out; WhatsApp disbursement; cross-sell module added to app and portal, giving instant checks with partner banks.
Partners: more than 40 financial partners and 14 lenders, per management.
Targeted corporate additions for FY27 were given in the Q&A, not as capex or capacity.
demand_pricing: Q4 FY26 EWA disbursal was about INR10 crore against guidance of INR11.5-12 crore for the quarter-end run rate; cross-sell disbursal was INR12 crore, now larger than EWA.
Corporate rejection rate is about 60%, based on CIBIL or banking checks; management attributed the slowdown to market volatility over the past three to four months.

Cross-sell yields: about 4% on personal loans, about 1% on gold loans, 1-1.25% on home loan or LAP; management said the blended yield changes every quarter. Management gave 1.3% as the cross-sell average when asked.

EWA revenue: management said about 6% of Q4 income came from EWA alone, while the presentation cited 8% for the full year on an EWA-overall basis; an analyst's Q4 EWA revenue estimate of INR70-80 lakh was not confirmed.
Gold loan syndication: INR375 crore disbursed in Q4 through ICICI, HDFC, RBL and Muthoot Finance.

Employee profile: average salary of EWA users about INR55,000-60,000; average loan INR25,000; cap INR1 lakh; minimum as low as INR100. Share of covered employees using EWA monthly is 15%; monthly repeat rate about 90%.

Corporate base: 214 corporates as of March 31, 2026, and about 185 active per Talin Aggarwal; June 2026 count not disclosed. Biggest corporate clients have about 1,000 employees each (Ind-Swift Labs, IDS Infotech).
Concentration controls: exposure capped at the lower of 50% of earned salary or INR1 lakh per employee, plus a company-level cap; corporate is paused for the month once its limit is hit.
Churn: seven corporates exited since programme inception, due to non-payment or liquidity risk.
SME book: INR111 crore, corrected from the analyst's INR120-130 crore figure.

qa_highlights.question: Has the EWA disbursement run rate slowed, given a guided INR11.5-12 crore for quarter-end?
qa_highlights.answer: Talin Aggarwal said Q4 EWA disbursal was INR10 crore because the market became highly volatile in the past three to four months, with corporate rejection near 60% on CIBIL or banking grounds.

qa_highlights.question: Is there any update on the FY27 profit guidance of INR32-40 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Aggarwal said FY26 EPS was INR4.36 and that he was fairly confident of crossing INR7 EPS in FY27 if all went well; he did not restate the INR32-40 crore range.

qa_highlights.question: Will the CRISIL upgrade lower the cost of funds?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Aggarwal said no reduction yet, that the company is getting many offers from financial institutions, and that an update would come shortly without a number.

qa_highlights.question: What were the incremental NPAs in Q4 from EWA and SME customers, and what is the NPA breakup?
qa_highlights.answer: Talin Aggarwal deferred the number to the books and to email. Sanjay Aggarwal said INR23 lakh was written off, of which INR8 lakh was business loan and the rest EWA; Gurmeet Kaur said no new customer was added to NPA in Q4.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the cross-sell book is underwritten on balance sheet versus distributed?
qa_highlights.answer: Talin Aggarwal said cross-sell is currently 100% distributed; loans of INR4-5 lakh are given from the company's book, with a corporate verbal guarantee and terms up to 12 months.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the rise in other expenses in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: Sanjay Aggarwal said provisions, a write-off of miscellaneous expenditure, CSR provision and a write-off of 50% of unavailable input tax credit (NBFC credit now 9% rather than 18%) were included.

risks_watch: Corporate rejection rate of about 60% and a volatile market could keep EWA disbursal below the INR11.5-12 crore run rate guided earlier.
Disclosure gaps: EWA revenue share (6% vs 8%), the cross-sell revenue split, the NPA breakup, the June 2026 corporate count and the AUM figures were deferred to email or a future update.
Cost of funds reduction after the CRISIL upgrade to BBB- is unconfirmed; watch for the promised announcement.
FY27 EPS target above INR7 versus INR4.36 in FY26 depends on the market; management's FY27 corporate-addition figures differ between answers (150-200 vs 120-150).
Recovery and write-off: a university-linked overdue was reported recovered; watch the FY27 NPA trend and post write-off recoveries (about INR6 lakh collected in April on a INR23 lakh write-off).
summary.management_tone: Confident on long-term growth but cautious on the near term, citing a volatile market and high corporate rejection rates. Evasive on several specifics: the June 2026 client count, cost-of-funds reduction, EWA revenue share and the NPA breakup, several of which were deferred to email or a future update.
key_quotes: We strongly believe that EWA continues to be scalable and a recurring use platform with strong long-term growth potential driven by increasing focus on employee financial wellness and digital value-added solutions.
The market is very finicky, or maybe I should say the market has become highly volatile in the past three to four months.
